question: Two distinct grades of rice, one priced at ₹80 per kilogram and the other at ₹120 per kilogram, are amalgamated in an undisclosed proportion. The resultant blend is retailied at ₹132 per kilogram, securing a profit margin of 20% on the overall cost price. Determine the precise ratio in which the two rice varieties were intermingled.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Mean Cost Price = Selling Price × [100 ÷ (100 + Profit%)]

Mean Cost Price = 132 × (100 ÷ 120) = ₹110/kg

Using Alligation Cross-Multiplication directly:

Quantity Ratio = (120 − 110) : (110 − 80)

Quantity Ratio = 10 : 30 = 1 : 3

**∴ The correct answer is 1 : 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost price of Grade 1 rice (CP₁) = ₹80/kg

Cost price of Grade 2 rice (CP₂) = ₹120/kg

Selling price of the mixture (SP) = ₹132/kg

Overall profit margin = 20%

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = (SP × 100) ÷ (100 + Profit%)

Alligation Ratio = (CP₂ − Mean CP) : (Mean CP − CP₁)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Mean CP of mixture = (132 × 100) ÷ (100 + 20)

⇒ Mean CP = 13200 ÷ 120 = ₹110/kg

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rule of Alligation

It allows finding the specific ratio in which two or more ingredients at given prices must be mixed to produce a mixture of a desired average price. Ratio = (Dearer Price − Mean Price) : (Mean Price − Cheaper Price).

Mean Price Concept

The cost price of a unit quantity of the mixture is called its mean price. When using the alligation method, always ensure that all values (CP₁, CP₂, and Mean Price) are purely Cost Prices. Never use Selling Price directly in the alligation cross.

Repeated Replacement

If a vessel contains 'x' units of a pure liquid and 'y' units are taken out and replaced by water 'n' times, the quantity of pure liquid remaining = x × (1 − y ÷ x)ⁿ.
